searchText: first congratulations This channel is for discussing proposed EVM changes, including all the ones proposed as EIPs for Eth1. First useful message, could be pinned ^ 👏 🙇‍♂️ To continue from previous room: I'm analyzing all contract code at block `9666637`. I dumped out all code (22G), and am now doing a filtering: only code containing - At least one `JUMP` or `JUMPI`, - At least one `BEGINSUB` (0xB2) - And a `JUMPDEST` _after_ the `BEGINSUB` IIUC, these are the contracts that would get bitten if we were to implement the new proposed subroutine-version by axic/pawel Afaict, the affected contracts are 'data', and the few I've looked at would exit after at most a few steps, due to invalid opcode and/or insufficient stack depth for an operation how do we have `BEGINSUB` on the mainnet? I thought it was not activated yet? Remember: EVM has no validation so random bytes can be considered opcodes And with subroutines we are giving meaning to one of those random bytes. <@!211091239112671234> do you have a list of these contracts? I soon will.. it's still running actually, I won't have a list of the addresses, only the `code, codeHash, balance, sha3(address)` I'll plop it into a gist https://gist.github.com/holiman/2cc4ccf268bd45901aec741e06288cc4 (the gist becomes truncated when you view it, but there's a link to the full gist from there) On line 41/42 contracts start with `0xff` which is selfdestruct. Are those data contracts? The ones starting with `60806040` are likely solidity, the others are unlikely solidity 🙂 Took a random one (line 3) and the only beginsub is in the "solidity metadata". A script should help: check if the bytecode ends in solidity metadata and if the begindata falls into that region, consider it "safe". We could probably remove the bulk of them by filtering any which will error out in the first couple of steps But we can't disregard non-solidity, since, y'know, there are other ways to code 🙂 Sure, but getting rid of these solidity cases should reduce the sample size 🙂 Oh I thought you meant that we could ignore the 'data'-contracts and focus on the solidity ones... now I understand Anyway, it's only `438` contracts, so pretty easy to script/filter on a laptop Looked at all the non-solidity looking ones on the truncated gist page (~25 of them) and all of them seem to be data contracts (because they have gibberish opcodes at the beginning) Out of `438`, we can remove `133` as obvious data-contracts which fail at first opcode. Remaining `305` mostly start with a PUSH1 Did you push the reduced list? https://gist.github.com/holiman/bd971272123bd01248f65b2f161bbb1a Maybe another 10-15 can be discarded by looking at the next op, and filtering a bit more aggressively on the first (a few slipped by me) But I estimate there's about ~290 solidity contracts Did a metadata decoding run on these. Fun act: A lot of them are Solidity pre-0.5.0. And a bunch of them have the experimental flag set. There is only two compiled with 0.6.x. Out of your list, only 167 don't have the BEGINSUB within the solidity metadata. Including 70 which don't have a metadata (so probably not solidity). They are actually solidity (at least set the "free memory") just are stripped. https://gist.github.com/axic/d03cfa1155554083999e858f375e21b7 A lot of them may have a valid first opcode (but would halt anyway, such as CODECOPY as first instruction) or have an invalid second opcode. I won't do that filtering now, but suggest it as the next step.

excerpts.content:
To continue from previous room: I'm analyzing all contract code at block `9666637`. I dumped out all code (22G), and am now doing a filtering: only code containing 

- At least one `JUMP` or `JUMPI`,
- At least one `BEGINSUB` (0xB2)
- And a `JUMPDEST` _after_ the `BEGINSUB`

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: IIUC, these are the contracts that would get bitten if we were to implement the new proposed subroutine-version by axic/pawel

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Afaict, the affected contracts are 'data', and the few I've looked at would exit after at most a few steps, due to invalid opcode and/or insufficient stack depth for an operation
